cells.tense: You're holding what's yours to hold, and you're still open while you do it.
cells.ask: Let one thing reach you today without deciding yet what it means
cells.core:
There's weight on you and it hasn't closed you. You take what people bring and you stay in touch with them even while you're under something yourself. That combination is harder than either one alone, and it makes the room steadier than you'd guess. What you let in tends to stay with you, and it stays because you didn't rush to name it.

That openness is the ground, and it can go further. What's ready next is letting what you feel keep deepening instead of settling into a verdict. Notice one thing that moves you today, and leave it open at the end.
cells.sheetLine: You stay open while you carry, and it holds.
cells.verb: opening to feel what's arriving before you know what it is
cells.place: where you carry what has to be carried

cells.tense: You're braced for what's coming, so the opening gets spent on getting ready.
cells.ask: Take what's actually on you today and do only today's part of it, then stop
cells.core:
Holding steady here means staying with what's in front of you. You take the day as it comes, you don't pick up tomorrow in advance, and the strength shows in holding what's real right now. Nothing gets carried that hasn't been handed to you yet.

Right now it's gone the other way. You're bracing for what hasn't happened, and the bracing turns into motion — arranging, pushing, making sure — so the openness you started with becomes a job. You're carrying more than what's here because you've already taken on what might be. Set down the weight you picked up ahead of time. Put your whole hand on one thing that's actually yours to do.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying what hasn't arrived yet.

cells.tense: You're standing at a door that's already behind you, holding what was there.
cells.ask: Let one thing in today that has nothing to do with what you're already holding
cells.core:
Holding well looks like taking the day as it comes — the load in your hands right now, nothing added, nothing saved. That's not effort. It's being here while it moves through. People reach you easily when you're like this, and what they bring doesn't have to get past anything.

The arms are full of something else today. What's in front of you goes unheld, and what's open in you doesn't get to meet it. The strength to carry is there. It has turned toward what's already over and away from what's actually on you. Let one thing reach you that you haven't rehearsed, and hold only what's here.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding what's behind you instead of what's here.
cells.verb: opening to feel what's arriving before you know what it is

cells.tense: You're carrying more than you'd say you are, and you call it just what the day requires.
cells.ask: Say once, out loud, that carrying one particular thing is a choice you've been making
cells.core:
When this is clear, you know what you're choosing to hold. You can feel the difference between what's actually yours and what you picked up on the way, and that knowing doesn't need to argue for itself — it lands. There's no confusion about which weight is which.

Most of the time it runs without you saying so. You make room for what people need, you keep going when it's heavy, and you describe it as the situation rather than something you're doing. The carrying is real and it's yours, and it's been getting no owner. Admit one thing you carry as a choice rather than a weight that fell on you.
cells.sheetLine: You're already choosing to carry it, and you never claimed it.
